newsitem.title: UK: Euro fuel oil softens as ARA barges sold below $80.
newsitem.headline: Euro fuel oil softens as ARA barges sold below $80.

text.p: European fuel oil markets were softer on Tuesday with high sulphur barge values slipping below the $80 mark on aggressive selling, traders said.

While barges were sold at $81 and $80 a tonne for next month delivery, one dealer traded prompt material for $78 a tonne and said he wanted to clear his tanks by end-month to make way for Russian material.
"There was some 10kt of business done yesterday at around $80-$81 and that set the tone for the downswing today," said one trader. Bunker demand was thin.
Opinions varied as to how much Russian material was around.
While one dealer said the flow of cracked fuel from St. Petersburg was pushing prices down, another complained he could find no mazut to buy.
One percent was quiet, with swaps steady at $96/$96.50, little business being talked and availability limited until well into June.
High sulphur cargoes were quiet, with numbers tracking softer barge quotes.
Good quality Russian straight-run cargoes were still scarce and attracting solid premiums
